ev.q: During March 2024, seven women experienced illness after receiving botulinum toxin injections in nonmedical settings; four were hospitalized.
All patients sought health care for their illness; four were hospitalized, and two were monitored in intensive care units.
All patients reported receiving cosmetic BoNT injections in nonmedical settings a median of 3 days (range = 2–20 days) before symptom onset.
Reported signs and symptoms included ptosis, dry mouth, dysphagia, shortness of breath, and weakness ( Table )

public_health_question.v: What were the characteristics of illnesses after cosmetic injection of presumed counterfeit botulinum toxin in nonmedical settings, and which products were implicated?

ev.q: A multistate investigation, which included the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and CDC, sought to characterize these illnesses and identify implicated BoNT products.

conditions.v: botulism-like illness after cosmetic botulinum toxin injection

ev.q: Illnesses After Administration of Presumed Counterfeit Botulinum Toxin in Nonmedical Settings
Seven persons experienced illness consistent with local and possible distant spread of BoNT after injection of presumed counterfeit BoNT product
A multistate investigation, which included the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and CDC, sought to characterize these illnesses and identify implicated BoNT products.
NYC DOHMH identified three patients, and TDH identified four (including one Kentucky resident who was admitted to a Tennessee hospital).
Health department staff members interviewed patients and reviewed medical records
Tennessee and New York City, March 2024

equity.level_reason: No social-position dimension is analyzed; sex and age only describe the seven patients.

level_alternative.reason: Unlicensed administration and low-cost or overseas products could be read as access-related descriptors, but they are not framed as social position.
